name: Confluence
description: Let agents find and read Confluence pages in the spaces you choose, such as release checklists, runbooks and sign-off pages. For release readiness checks and go/no-go summaries.
identity: An Atlassian service account named "{brand.microsoft.appName}" with OAuth 2.0 credentials. It uses no Confluence seat and reads only the spaces it is given.

setup.title: Create a service account with Confluence access
setup.body: In Atlassian Administration, create a service account named "{brand.microsoft.appName}". When it asks you to select an app role, set Confluence to User and leave every other app on None. If you already made one for Jira, you can use it and add the Confluence role.

link.label: Atlassian: create OAuth 2.0 credentials for service accounts

click: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > Create service account
Select app role: Confluence > User (every other app: None) > Create

setup.title: Let it view the spaces agents should read
setup.body: Give the service account the View permission in each space agents should read, and nothing more. You can narrow each agent to some of those spaces here later.
click: In each space: Space settings > Users > Add people > {brand.microsoft.appName} > View only

setup.title: Create OAuth 2.0 credentials
setup.body: On the service account, select Create credentials, then OAuth 2.0, and select exactly these scopes. Copy the client ID and secret: Atlassian shows the secret only once.
click: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > {brand.microsoft.appName} > Create credentials > OAuth 2.0 > Next
Scopes: read:page:confluence and read:space:confluence > Next > Create

setup.title: Find your site's cloud ID
setup.body: Atlassian calls your site by an ID. Open the address below with your site's name in place of your-company: the cloudId it shows goes in the form.
click: Open https://your-company.atlassian.net/_edge/tenant_info in your browser and copy cloudId.

capabilities.label: Read pages
capabilities.description: List spaces, list a space's pages by title, and read a page with its content.
capabilities.note: Read-only. Reaches the spaces the service account may view unless you keep a key to chosen spaces.

limits.label: Spaces
limits.help: Optional: only pages in these spaces, by space id (listed under Spaces after connecting). Leave empty for every space the service account may view.

verify.label: Confluence spaces
verify.ifEmpty: The service account cannot view any space yet: give it View in the spaces agents should read.

revoke: In Atlassian Administration, go to Directory > Service accounts, select {brand.microsoft.appName} and delete its OAuth 2.0 credentials, or remove its Confluence role. Agents lose access to Confluence within the hour, when their last token expires.

tools.name: confluence_list_spaces
tools.description: List spaces with their id, key and name, or find some by key. Pass next from the answer as cursor for the next page.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous answer

tools.name: confluence_list_pages
tools.description: List pages in some spaces, optionally only those with a given title, newest first. Pass next from the answer as cursor for the next page.

title.description: Only pages with exactly this title

cursor.description: The next value of the previous answer

tools.name: confluence_get_page
tools.description: Read one page with its content, in Confluence's storage format (XHTML) by default.
